definition.name: Seismic Globe
definition.description: Fetches the USGS M2.5+ seven-day feed and builds a bounded 3D globe plus a self-contained animated HTML Response with a 30-second earthquake replay, timed spikes, surface rings, controls, and live event metadata for a fork.io site.

params.text:
# Seismic Globe

USGS M2.5+ earthquakes / past seven days / at most 1,000 newest valid events.

**Spike height = magnitude. Color = depth.**

- Mint: depth <70 km
- Amber: depth 70 to <300 km
- Rose: depth 300+ km

Spikes start at the globe surface and extend outward. They are symbols, not literal earthquake height, rupture size, or depth. Height = 0.25 x magnitude - 0.5 scene units; globe radius = 3. This linear visual encoding is not an energy scale.

Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, right-drag to pan. The HTML Response starts automatically and compresses event timestamps into 30 seconds. Its controls pause, replay, reset, or select a 15/30/60-second duration. Each arrival pulses its spike, emits concentric surface rings, and updates the event metadata card. The native 3D panel keeps the bounded scene and slow globe rotation, but displays the earthquake snapshot statically. Run again for a new snapshot.

The Data Table retains ID, place, magnitude, depth, timestamp (Unix milliseconds) and event URL. Spikes remain linked to the table for selection and inspection. Empty depth bands produce no spikes.

The dotted graticule is spaced at 30 degrees. Coastline dots are a sampled reference, not a detailed basemap.

Coordinates: +Y north, +X at longitude 0 on the equator, -Z at longitude 90 east. Camera starts over the eastern Pacific. All positions and rotations are authored by the graph, not earthquake-specific renderer code.

[USGS feed format](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/geojson.php) | [Natural Earth coastline / public domain](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/about/terms-of-use/)
